boundaries: IDs are unique within one CLI invocation; Log/debug payloads keep their existing format and do not all carry IDs. This is a human status stream, not the future structured report protocol.
Common input options are reapplied at each admission; queued source/variable files can change externally. Files, cwd/environment, stdout/stderr, and native/filesystem pools are process resources.

The scheduler retains at most jobs run tasks/identity records plus one reporting record. CLI argument storage is outside per-run interpreter budgets. Per-run quotas do not establish a cross-run process-memory/output ceiling.

Normal failure finishes siblings. Reporter failure stops further admission, suppresses later records, drains admitted runs, and returns failure; it cannot promise delivery through a broken destination.

Blocking reads/callbacks must return before drain completes. Whole-run shutdown bounds, signal/listener cancellation, foreign adapters, structured reports, per-run manifests, and release performance/stress acceptance remain open.
